topic: understanding the concept of arc length and sector area of a circle

easy.text: The arc length of a circle refers to:

options.text: The distance along a curved portion (arc) of the circle's circumference
options.feedback: Correct -- arc length measures the curved distance between two points along a circle's edge, corresponding to a specific central angle.

options.text: The straight-line distance across the entire circle
options.feedback: That describes the DIAMETER, not arc length, which specifically measures a CURVED distance along the circle's edge, not a straight line across it.

options.text: The total area enclosed within the circle
options.feedback: That describes the circle's AREA, not arc length, which specifically measures a linear distance along the curved edge, not an enclosed area.

options.text: The exact center point of the circle
options.feedback: Arc length doesn't refer to a specific point at all -- it's a distance measurement along a portion of the circle's curved boundary.

medium.text: A circle has a radius of 10 cm. What is the arc length corresponding to a 90-degree central angle? (Use the formula: arc length = (angle/360) × 2πr, with π≈3.14)

options.feedback: This is the FULL circumference (2πr) of the circle, without applying the (90/360) fraction for just this specific arc portion.
This is HALF the circumference (corresponding to 180 degrees), not the correct arc length for a 90-degree angle.
This is just the radius value itself, not the correctly calculated arc length using the given formula.

hard.text: A circular pizza has a radius of 12 inches. What is the AREA of a single slice (sector) that spans a 45-degree central angle? (Use: sector area = (angle/360) × πr², with π≈3.14)

options.feedback: This is the area of the ENTIRE pizza (πr²), without applying the (45/360) fraction for just this specific slice.
This would correspond to a 90-degree slice (1/4 of the pizza), not the specified 45-degree slice.
This is just the radius value itself, not the correctly calculated sector area using the given formula.

easy.hard: This measurement quantifies the curvilinear distance spanning a designated portion of a circle's outer boundary.
easy.medium: This is the distance along a curved piece of the circle's outer edge.
easy.easy: This is the distance along a curved piece of the circle's edge.

medium.hard: Determine what fraction of the full circumference corresponds to the given central angle, then apply that fraction to the total circumference value.
medium.medium: Figure out what fraction of the full circle 90 degrees represents (90/360), then apply that fraction to the total circumference.
medium.easy: 90/360 is 1/4. The full circumference is 62.8, so 1/4 of that is 15.7.

hard.hard: Determine what fraction of the total circle area corresponds to the given central angle, then apply that fraction to the total circle area value.
hard.medium: Figure out what fraction of the full circle 45 degrees represents (45/360), then apply that fraction to the total circle area.
hard.easy: 45/360 is 1/8. The full circle area is 452.16, so 1/8 of that is 56.52.
